body.estimand_functional: \(C_n=\{\theta\in K:\sqrt n\,\widehat q_n(\theta)/(\widehat\sigma_n(\theta)\vee n^{-1})\leq\widehat c_{1-\eta}\}\), with uniform whole-identified-set coverage over the uniformly regular fixed-relevance subclass \(\mathcal P_W\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_W}\{\sqrt{\delta(P)}+n^{-1/4}\}E_P[d_{\to}\{C_n,\Theta_I(P)\}]=O(n^{-1/2})\); in particular, contact loss is \(n^{-1/4}\) and fixed-interior loss is \(n^{-1/2}\).

sampling_model.design: Observational i.i.d. triangular arrays in the centered linear Watson leaky-instrument SEM.
sampling_model.units: Independent draws \(W_i=(Z_i^{\prime},X_i,Y_i)^{\prime}\) with fixed \(d\) and uniformly bounded eighth moments.
sampling_model.treatment: Continuous treatment \(X_i\) with reduced-form relevance \(\|\beta(P)\|_2\geq c_{\beta}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; weak instruments are excluded by the fixed relevance bound.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The covariance blocks use the measurable ridge inverse \(R_n(S)=(S+n^{-2}I_d)^{-1}\) on every original and bootstrap sample. Reduced-form vectors, the regularized score derivative, and its variance are then sample plug-ins; one Gaussian multiplier process supplies the critical value without conditioning on empirical invertibility. The retained bootstrap uses exactly \(B_n\to\infty\) conditionally independent Efron \(n\)-out-of-\(n\) candidates, strict positive-slack retention, an empirical endpoint-pair law, and a Dirac fallback at the original totalized endpoint pair when no candidate is retained.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The resulting bootstrap distributions are asymptotically valid and practically useful.
There exist no locally asymptotically unbiased estimators and no regular estimators for the stated nondifferentiable functionals.
Random sets can cover the entire identified set uniformly over a class of laws.
Bootstrap approximation of an estimated local parameter space yields uniformly valid tests in constrained moment models.
Gaussian multiplier bootstrap consistently estimates maxima of sums of high-dimensional random vectors under stated conditions.
Full differentiability is necessary and sufficient for standard-bootstrap consistency under a Gaussian first-stage limit.
The nonparametric bootstrap is inconsistent for the boundary-constrained normal-mean estimator.
Test inversion gives uniformly valid inference for root-\(n\) constrained optimization estimators drifting toward a boundary.

body.tldr: Taking Watson et al.'s unrestricted raw \(p=2\) interval as a published input, this note intersects it with \(K\) and studies tangent contact. The total positive-part plug-in endpoints have a fourth-root Gaussian law, while the fully specified feasibility-retained bootstrap converges to a random truncated kernel and is not contact-uniform. The uniform multiplier-coupling theorem, now fully discharged, makes inversion before the square-root map uniformly cover the whole identified set on the strict uniformly regular fixed-relevance subclass \(\mathcal P_W\). Its exact continuous elbow yields \(n^{-1/4}\) contact loss and \(n^{-1/2}\) fixed-interior loss under the same rule. The Gaussian bootstrap counterexample and the minimax converse use laws inside the published model and therefore transfer upward to Watson et al.'s broader \(p=2\) class; the upper hull guarantee is not claimed for that unrestricted class.

project_justification.gap: Watson et al.'s Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.7 provide the \(p=2\) sharp quadratic sublevel-set identity and its raw endpoint representation at nonnegative slack, and their Theorem 4 supplies a feasibility-retained bootstrap workflow. They do not derive the fourth-root contact law, the random retained-resample kernel for the fully specified finite Monte Carlo algorithm, contact-uniform validity, a whole-identified-set score hull, or a minimax loss frontier. Existing boundary and directional-bootstrap theory does not supply those leaky-IV results.
project_justification.niche: The published scalar quadratic score remains regular at tangent contact even though the endpoint square root is only half-Hölder. Calibrating the score before endpoint transformation creates a route to uniform set inference and makes both contact and interior local minimax geometry explicit.
project_justification.fill: The project keeps the causal target distinct from its observed-law score representation, takes Watson et al.'s unrestricted raw interval as a published input, and imposes the intersection with \(K\) itself. It derives the fourth-root contact law and the retained random kernel for an exact Efron algorithm, proves nonuniformity for that named workflow, and constructs an every-sample multiplier score hull using a common ridge convention. The uniform multiplier theorem is fully discharged and gives whole-set coverage throughout the strict uniformly regular fixed-relevance subclass \(\mathcal P_W\), while the exact score-set modulus gives a continuous loss elbow and matched contact and interior Gaussian LAN frontiers. The bootstrap counterexample and converse transfer to the broader published \(p=2\) model, but the upper guarantee does not.

body.related_work: Watson et al. (2024, Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.7) supply the unrestricted raw \(p=2\) sharp interval; intersection with \(K\) is imposed by this note. Their Theorem 4 supplies the feasibility-retained endpoint-bootstrap workflow. The exact finite-\(B_n\) Efron algorithm, its negligible zero-retention fallback, the contact endpoint law, retained random kernel, nonuniformity result, score hull, continuous loss elbow, and matched frontiers are not attributed to that paper. Andrews (2000) supplies local boundary-sequence logic, and Fang and Santos (2019) distinguish a regular Gaussian primitive from a nonsmooth transform. Romano and Shaikh (2010) inform the whole-identified-set coverage criterion; Chernozhukov, Newey, and Santos (2023) inform constrained-score inversion; and Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013) inform multiplier and anti-concentration arguments. The finite-dimensional quadratic-score proof adapted here fully discharged the paper's multiplier question, but only on the strict uniformly regular subclass \(\mathcal P_W\). Hirano and Porter (2012) rule out regular estimation of nondifferentiable functionals; the present Gaussian LAN calculations sharpen that diagnosis to matched fourth-root and root-\(n\) directed-Hausdorff frontiers. Hong and Li's numerical bootstrap regularizes inference for nondifferentiable maps through a tuning/perturbation scheme; it does not deliver the present tuning-free inversion of the regular quadratic score, whole-identified-set coverage, or its explicit contact-to-interior loss elbow. Li (2025) uses a proximal bootstrap and test inversion to obtain uniformly valid inference for root-\(n\) constrained optimization estimators drifting toward a boundary. That result is relevant because both approaches invert a constraint-facing statistic rather than bootstrap a nonsmooth endpoint directly, but it neither analyzes this half-Holder quadratic-contact endpoint map nor supplies the present single multiplier score hull's whole-identified-set coverage and matched fourth-root-to-root-\(n\) directed-loss elbow. Takatsu and Kuchibhotla provide general local-minimax lower-bound tools for nonsmooth and irregular functionals; the Gaussian LAN converses here are problem-specific two-law-testing counterparts matched to the constructive score-hull upper rates. Staiger and Stock study weak-instrument sequences in which first-stage relevance can vanish, whereas the upper score-hull theorem here assumes relevance uniformly bounded away from zero; no weak-IV robustness is claimed. The bootstrap counterexample and converse witnesses belong to Watson et al.'s broader published \(p=2\) model, whereas the upper hull guarantee does not extend beyond \(\mathcal P_W\).
body.technical_internal_limitation: The uniform upper theorem is deliberately limited to the strict subclass \(\mathcal P_W\): fixed dimension, known leakage radius, uniform covariance conditioning, a bounded eighth moment, score-variance bounds, parameter-space margin, and fixed relevance are load-bearing. It does not establish a multiplier approximation for Watson et al.'s unrestricted \(p=2\) class, weak instruments, growing dimension, unknown leakage radius, or contact with the boundary of \(K\). The expected-loss elbow also uses the theorem's integrable root-\(n\) score-band radius; distributional coupling alone would give coverage but not the displayed risk bound. The Gaussian bootstrap nonuniformity witness and the minimax converses require none of that upward extension of the upper theorem and remain valid in the broader published class.
body.honest_scope: Watson et al.'s Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.7 supply the unrestricted raw \(p=2\) interval. This note separately restricts the target to \(K\), so the identified set is the \(K\)-restricted score sublevel set and the raw square-root endpoints are used only at nonnegative slack. The parameter margin removes \(K\)-truncation on the maintained contact-local and fixed-interior regimes. The uniform multiplier-coupling theorem is fully discharged and proves whole-set coverage plus the continuous expected-loss elbow on the strict uniformly regular fixed-relevance subclass \(\mathcal P_W\). That upper theorem uses fixed \(d\), known scalar leakage radius, uniformly conditioned covariance, bounded eighth moments, nondegenerate score variance, compact parameter margin, and relevance bounded away from zero; it is not asserted for Watson et al.'s unrestricted class. By contrast, the explicit Gaussian bootstrap counterexample and both minimax lower-bound paths lie within the published model, so those negative and converse conclusions transfer upward. All finite-sample covariance operations use the stated ridge convention, and the directed loss is defined when a random hull is empty.
